skill.name: docker-workflow
skill.description: Docker workflow guidance for building, optimizing, debugging, and deploying containerized applications with Dockerfiles and Docker Compose.
skill.summary: Build, optimize, debug, and deploy Docker containers with practical templates and helper commands.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate Docker workflow material, and many static findings are Markdown or Docker-template false positives. Real concerns remain around copyable default credentials, inline connection strings, a helper command that prints container environments, and forced Docker cleanup operations.

remediation.issue: Default credentials and inline secrets appear in Docker Compose examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sample passwords and SECRET_KEY defaults with placeholders, require .env.example values, and state that real secrets must come from a secret manager or local untracked env file.

remediation.issue: The helper script can print all container environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the env command or redact common secret names such as TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, and DATABASE_URL by default.

remediation.issue: The cleanup command force-prunes volumes and networks.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit confirmation flag for destructive cleanup and separate volume pruning from routine cleanup.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes sudo package installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that users should verify package sources and prefer official Docker installation instructions for their platform before running privileged commands.

semantic_findings.title: Helper command can print container secrets
semantic_findings.description: The helper exposes an env command that runs docker exec "$container" env and sorts the output. This can reveal API keys, passwords, and tokens stored in container environment variables.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command directly prints all environment variables from a running container. Container environments commonly contain secrets in Docker workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Cleanup command removes Docker resources without confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup command prunes stopped containers, dangling images, unused volumes, and unused networks with force flags. This can delete local state or development data if users run it casually.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script uses docker container/image/volume/network prune -f. These are legitimate maintenance commands, but forced volume pruning can remove local data.

semantic_findings.title: Example stack includes default administrative passwords
semantic_findings.description: The compose example includes default passwords such as password, admin, and redispassword for database, message queue, Redis, Grafana, and pgAdmin services. Users may copy these examples into exposed environments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple services define obvious default credentials in a full-stack compose file. The file is an example, but it also publishes services on host ports.

content.value_statement: Container setup often fails because Dockerfiles, compose files, and debugging steps are scattered. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured Docker workflow with templates and operational checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of .dockerignore files, multi-stage Dockerfiles, and docker-compose configurations.
Provides example Dockerfiles for Node.js, Python, Go, Java, Rust, and development containers.
Explains image optimization through layer caching, smaller base images, BuildKit, and cleanup patterns.
Includes a Bash helper for Docker health checks, inspection, logs, shell access, image sizing, backups, and cleanup.
Documents production practices such as non-root users, health checks, restart policies, reverse proxies, and monitoring services.
limitations: It does not inspect your real application dependencies unless you provide the project context.
The examples require review before production use because they include placeholder credentials and broad port exposure.
The helper script assumes local Docker access and may not match managed container platforms.
It does not replace image vulnerability scanners or infrastructure policy checks.

use_cases.title: Containerize a web application
use_cases.description: Create a Dockerfile, .dockerignore, and compose stack for a frontend, backend, database, and cache.

use_cases.title: Debug a failing container
use_cases.description: Use health checks, logs, inspection, shell access, port mappings, and network checks to find runtime issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare images for deployment
use_cases.description: Apply multi-stage builds, non-root users, health checks, restart policies, and image size reduction before release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic Docker setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the docker-workflow skill to create a Dockerfile, .dockerignore, and docker-compose.yml for this application. Explain each file in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Add development compose support
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the docker-workflow skill to design a Docker Compose development environment with hot reload, service dependencies, and safe environment variable handling.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an existing image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the docker-workflow skill to review my Dockerfile for layer caching, image size, dependency separation, and non-root runtime improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan production container deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the docker-workflow skill to prepare this Docker setup for production. Include health checks, restart policy, secret handling, networking, monitoring, and rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: Create Docker files for a Node.js API with PostgreSQL.
output: A multi-stage Node.js Dockerfile with dependency caching and a non-root runtime user.
A docker-compose service layout for the app and PostgreSQL with health checks.
A .dockerignore checklist that excludes dependencies, logs, build output, version control, and env files.

output_examples.input: My container starts and then exits.
output: A troubleshooting sequence that checks container status, logs, entrypoint behavior, and health check output.
Suggested docker commands to inspect configuration, run an interactive shell, and verify required environment variables.

output_examples.input: Make this image smaller and safer.
output: Recommendations to use a smaller base image, split build and runtime stages, remove build tools, and pin image versions.
Security checks for non-root users, minimal packages, vulnerability scanning, and secret exclusion.

best_practices: Replace all example credentials before running compose files outside a private local environment.
Review generated Docker commands before execution, especially cleanup, shell, backup, and deployment commands.
Pair this skill with image scanning and policy checks before publishing production images.
anti_patterns: Do not copy default passwords from example compose files into shared or production environments.
Do not run forced Docker cleanup commands when local volumes may contain important data.
Do not store production secrets directly in Dockerfiles, compose files, or committed .env files.

faq.question: Does this skill create Dockerfiles for multiple languages?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance and examples for Node.js, Python, Go, Java, Rust, and generic development containers.

faq.question: Can it help with Docker Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers multi-service compose files, networks, volumes, dependencies, health checks, and environment-specific overrides.

faq.question: Is it safe to use the included examples directly?
faq.answer: Use them as templates only. Replace credentials, review exposed ports, and adjust networks before running them in shared environments.

faq.question: Does the helper script modify Docker state?
faq.answer: Yes. Some commands inspect state, while cleanup, restart, backup, and shell commands can change or expose local container state.

faq.question: Can this replace a vulnerability scanner?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance, but production images still need vulnerability scanning and policy review.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
